typed_relations.evidence_source: The subagent lifecycle (a parked subagent costs nothing; a resume keeps its context) is a fact about the harness, not a choice of Loudon's, and stays in auto-memory, labelled operator-env native. (_ops/Substrate Skill.md:216)

typed_relations.evidence_source: The palace's most finished instruments are samplers: [[Phoneme Choir]] and [[Talking Keyboard]] ... [[Splice Instrument Forge]] builds Ableton racks from Splice sounds on request. The topology is the simplest in the family and the most completely fixed; everything that varies lives in the content. (Synthesis Topologies.md:94)
typed_relations.evidence_target: [[Generative Preset Development]] navigates a fixed synth's parameters; this project navigates a fixed sampler's zones and a Set's slots. The same move, content instead of configuration. (Projects/Splice Instrument Forge.md:64)

typed_relations.evidence_source: FM depends on its ratio. At a whole-number carrier-to-modulator ratio its Bessel sidebands sit on the harmonic lattice, type 1 in disguise; at an irrational ratio its partials sit at k f_c + n f_m, a two-generator lattice, which is type 2 ([[Bessel Functions in Synthesis]]). (Three Kinds of Warp.md:97)
typed_relations.evidence_target: Both are right, and the ratio is the scope: whole numbers keep the series, anything else leaves it. (FM Synthesis.md:64)
typed_relations.rationale: The two pages now state the same scoped claim about FM's ratio from opposite ends, and the warp page's FM sentence points only at the Bessel maths, not at the instrument page that settled the question.

typed_relations.evidence_source: The seed was a specific frustration with FM synthesis. FM produces sidebands at C ± n·M — a comb whose teeth are always arithmetically related to the carrier/modulator ratio. (Projects/2D Torus Wavetable Synthesizer.md:55)
typed_relations.evidence_target: Ratio: how fast the modulator runs compared with the carrier. It decides where the new partials go. (FM Synthesis.md:43)
typed_relations.rationale: The project names FM as its seed, and the instrument it grew out of now has a page; emerged-from points the project back at its origin.

typed_relations.evidence_source: FM falls out for free. Because `duration` controls the phasor increment, audio-rate duration modulation is literally frequency modulation — the curvature engine is an FM operator whose carrier waveshape is itself a continuously-bendable parameter. Most FM operators have a fixed sine carrier. (Exponential Decay Curvature.md:105)
typed_relations.evidence_target: An operator is a sine oscillator with its own volume and its own envelope, nothing more. (FM Synthesis.md:37)
typed_relations.rationale: The curvature page claims its engine is an FM operator and defines itself against FM's fixed sine carrier, which is the definition the FM page gives.

typed_relations.evidence_source: Cosine of cosine modulation (the FM exponent): the c_n are Bessel functions, the famous Bessel-spectrum FM. FM is a Floquet system whose modulation spectrum happens to be Bessel-shaped. See [[Bessel Functions in Synthesis]]. (Projects/Floquet Time-Modulated Loops.md:273)
typed_relations.evidence_target: At a few hertz that push is vibrato. At audio rate it is timbre. (FM Synthesis.md:39)
typed_relations.rationale: Floquet already carries the label fm-is-a-floquet-system, but on its Bessel link, written before FM had a page; the claim is about the instrument, so it belongs on a link to FM (see the matching weak_links entry).

typed_relations.evidence_source: Not on the entry; in its own extracted text: 'Frequency modulation synthesis also starts with simple waveforms, but this time they are used to modulate(vary) the frequency of each other. When both waves are in the audio range(20hz-20,000 Hz) the results are surprising ... It is kind of an advanced additive synthesis' (Synthesis Notes (Loudon) — source — notes-text.txt:14-21)
typed_relations.evidence_target: Speed a vibrato up and, somewhere past 20 Hz, it stops being a wobble in the pitch and becomes a change in the tone. (FM Synthesis.md:33)
typed_relations.rationale: Loudon's notes open the oscillator chapter with a paragraph on FM that the entry's section list leaves out; one sentence on the entry naming it would carry a symmetric link that reaches both newcomers.

summary: Walked all seven newcomers two hops out from palace-map-full-2026-11-08 and searched the whole vault for each one's name and subject. I propose 14 links: 9 already have a sentence on the pointing page, and 5 need a sentence first (marked needs_sentence; they go to Loudon's eye). FM Synthesis is the clear case: four established pages (Three Kinds of Warp, 2D Torus, Exponential Decay Curvature, Floquet) talk about FM in sentences written before it had a page, and Floquet even carries the label fm-is-a-floquet-system on its link to Bessel. That link should be relabelled or retargeted. The thinnest newcomers are thin for honest reasons. Nothing in the palace talks about OCR yet, and only Lettering's open ask for a legibility judge reaches for one. Cycle 5 Explorer is mentioned nowhere outside its own bundle. Splice Instrument Forge's other mentions are in ledgers (Sentry, Closing Well), not entries. So those three stay below target unless Loudon writes the sentences. Three stale sentences turned up along the way that aren't links. Weaving Memory into the Palace:60 still asks whether Substrate Skill will grow an 'operating this environment' section, and it has one. Wavetable Oscillator:79 still says one of the FM lines 'needs its scope stated', which FM Synthesis:64 and Three Kinds of Warp:97 now settle. AI Partnership Philosophy § Claude's Configuration says values are 'configured in memory', which goes against Operator Memory's rule, unless it means claude.ai's memory; only Loudon knows which. The newcomers' own outbound links all read correctly; the only one I'd change is Cycle 5 Explorer → FOUR PILLARS (exemplifies → mirrors).
